title: U.S. House · Louisiana's 2nd District
area: New Orleans, Jefferson Parish, St. Bernard Parish and the River Parishes of southeast Louisiana.

context.text: Louisiana's 2026 U.S. House elections use a "majority vote" (all-party) system: every candidate, regardless of party, appears on one ballot on November 3, 2026. If no candidate wins a majority, the top two finishers advance to a December 12, 2026 general election. The partisan primary and runoff originally scheduled for May and June 2026 were canceled after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Louisiana v. Callais that the state's congressional map was an unconstitutional racial gerrymander, requiring a new map.

priorities.text: Site describes him as authoring or co-authoring laws focused on infrastructure, economic development, women's healthcare, criminal justice reform and reducing homelessness during his time in the Louisiana Legislature.
Describes himself as a steadfast advocate for civil rights, healthcare and environmental justice.

positions.summary: Statement on voting against a budget that did not extend ACA premium tax credits, calling the lapse unconscionable and warning against Medicaid cuts.
positions.quote: Not extending Affordable Care Act tax credits is unconscionable.

positions.summary: Said military action against Venezuela without congressional authorization was unconstitutional and that he voted for a war powers resolution.
positions.quote: The power to authorize the use of military force rests with Congress.

positions.summary: Statement during the House debate on the SAVE Act said the bill demands burdensome documentation and would make it harder for eligible Americans to vote.
positions.quote: This legislation is not only unnecessary — it is un-American. It demands burdensome documentation under the false pretense of preventing a problem that does not exist.

positions.summary: In remarks at a Democratic forum on immigration raids and mass deportations, criticized the planned Border Patrol sweep of the New Orleans area as a show of force rather than public safety.
positions.quote: What is being planned for our region is not real public safety. It is a political stunt wrapped in badges and guns.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and the House Homeland Security Committee in the 119th Congress; previously served on the Committees on Small Business and on Transportation and Infrastructure.
Elected 1st Vice Chairman of the Congressional Black Caucus and selected by House Democratic leadership as a Deputy Whip on the House floor.

priorities.text: Says her candidacy prioritizes an economic model favoring residents' well-being over corporate interests, including advocating for a livable wage tied to the true cost of living.
Wants to direct federal infrastructure funding to local needs such as fixing broken water mains and maintaining fire hydrants.
Campaigns on making housing affordable, targeting 80% of Area Median Income, and providing "Voucher Literacy" to help residents use housing benefits.
Campaign site lists three priorities: Louisiana's fair share of federal dollars, "Easier to Live Here" (insurance, housing, energy, groceries) and "Healthcare That Works".
Supports banning congressional stock trading and spending discipline and serious fiscal reform, per her campaign issues page.

positions.summary: Issues page says she opposes elective late-term abortion and supports exceptions, and that reproductive medical decisions belong to a woman and her physician.
positions.quote: reproductive medical decisions belong to a woman in consultation with her physician — not to politicians and not to the federal government. She supports exceptions involving rape, incest, and threats to the life or health of the mother.

statements.quote: Lisa opposes federal rent and price controls as the primary answer.
statements.context: On her campaign issues page, Housing affordability

statements.quote: She would focus on what actually limits supply — construction costs, insurance, financing, and the regulatory pile-up that makes building slow and expensive.
statements.context: On her campaign issues page, Housing affordability

statements.quote: I believe the federal government has both the authority and the responsibility to enforce federal immigration law, and I support securing the border.
statements.context: In a written answer on her campaign website

statements.quote: Congress has an obligation to protect access to essential healthcare while demanding that taxpayer dollars are spent effectively.
statements.context: In a written answer on her campaign website, on Medicaid

statements.quote: Lisa supports responsible domestic production, including offshore.
statements.context: On her campaign issues page, Energy and offshore production

priorities.text: Campaign site lists strengthening EMS as essential healthcare, protecting EMTs and paramedics, ending ambulance monopolies and bringing Louisiana's voice to Washington.
In his Ballotpedia survey, lists election security with ballot access, limits on eminent domain, and protecting Louisiana's aquifer.

statements.quote: The SAVE Act is about strengthening the verification of citizenship when registering to vote in federal elections.
statements.context: In his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

researchNotes: Lisa Ballay: positions from her campaign website, whose issue text is written in the third person. Walter Beach: one statement from his Ballotpedia survey and EMS-focused campaign site; remains minimal on the guide issues. Renada Collins: campaign site (RenadaCollinsForYou.org) did not load; Ballotpedia survey and Baton Rouge Press Club forum coverage (WBRZ, 2026-10-06) gave no stance on the guide issues. No campaign website or public statements were found for Peter Williams beyond his name, party and the forum, where he said he wants better representation for middle-class families. Renada Collins is listed as "No Party" in the Louisiana Illuminator voter guide and The Green Papers district list (changed from D on 2026-10-19). No campaign website or public statements were found for Lisa Ballay beyond her name and Libertarian ballot line. Biographies for Peter Williams, Walter Beach and Renada Collins come from their self-reported Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey answers.
